core_obligations: Reduce to the affine case Spec(B) -> Spec(A) with A -> B finite and of finite presentation, and write F = M-tilde (proof lines 2326-2330).
Apply the algebra lemma to see that M is finitely presented over B exactly when it is over A (proof lines 2331-2333).
Use the dictionary between finite presentation of a module and of its associated sheaf to conclude (proof lines 2334-2336).
difficulty_reason: For a finite morphism f of finite presentation and a quasi-coherent O_X-module F, the lemma asserts that F is of finite presentation if and only if f_* F is (statement lines 2315-2323). The proof reduces affinely: a finite morphism is affine, so one is reduced to Spec(B) -> Spec(A) with A -> B finite and finitely presented, and F = M-tilde for a B-module M; the algebraic content is that M is finitely presented over B exactly when it is finitely presented over A, which is the extension lemma, after which the standard dictionary between finite presentation of a module and of its associated sheaf gives the claim (proof lines 2325-2336). The level is H2: the reduction is short but the equivalence being invoked is the substantive point and it is named.
